content_html:
Epistemic Boundary — I Ching × Quantum Measurement

The epistemic boundary is the threshold between potential and manifestation. In both I Ching divination and quantum measurement, knowledge arises through an interaction that both reveals and constrains: by making one aspect determinate, others recede. The boundary is therefore not ignorance to be eliminated but a constitutive feature of how knowing becomes possible.

An epistemic boundary is the limit of what can be known or meaningfully stated within a framework of observation. It is a conceptual horizon—not a physical barrier—where potentiality lies on one side and determinate, communicable outcomes lie on the other.

Term Concise Meaning Illustration
Epistemic About knowledge: its scope, justification, conditions What our theories and instruments allow us to say
Boundary A limit or horizon in a system of understanding Where descriptions stop being well-defined

I Ching: Boundary Between Dao and Interpretation

In the I Ching, prior to casting, all hexagrams are latent—a correlative field of possibilities. The casting act (with coins or stalks) is a crossing of the epistemic boundary: it selects one pattern that becomes interpretable within the inquirer’s situation (lifeworld and intention). Classical commentaries repeatedly stress that the Dao exceeds what can be fully said; the Book is a prompt to insight, not a final ontology.

Quantum Measurement: Boundary Between Superposition and Outcome

In quantum theory, the wavefunction encodes potentialities (superposed alternatives). A measurement crosses the epistemic boundary: a specific eigenvalue/state becomes actual, and complementary quantities become inaccessible within that context. The uncertainty principle formalizes this epistemic limit.

Parallel Structure

Aspect I Ching (Divination) Quantum Mechanics (Measurement) Shared Meaning
Domain of Potential Dao; all hexagrams latent Wavefunction; superposition Possibility before encounter
Act Crossing Boundary Casting & interpretation Measurement & collapse Interaction yields knowable outcome
Context-Dependence Question, lifeworld, commentary Observable chosen, apparatus, prep What appears is conditioned by setup
Intrinsic Limits The Dao cannot be fully spoken Uncertainty; complementarity Built-in horizon of knowability

Philosophical Resonance

Tradition Formulation of the Boundary Note
Daoism “The Dao that can be spoken is not the eternal Dao.” Limits of naming; openness of the source.
Kant Phenomena vs. noumena Things-in-themselves beyond possible experience.
Phenomenology Appearance is horizon-bound We meet phenomena, not unmediated reality.
Bohr/Heisenberg Complementarity & uncertainty Physics describes what we can say about nature.
